extracted.intended_audience: academic researchers and faculty in advertising/marketing seeking foundation research grants; university research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation standards for awarding A.A.A.A. Educational Foundation research grants supporting academic research in advertising, marketing, communications, and consumer behavior. Covers selection criteria, eligibility, administrative/financial restrictions, reporting, and expectations about research quality and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity and realism of approach to proposed research
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants were awarded on the basis of seven criteria: (1) Validity and realism of approach to proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluator should judge whether the proposed research design and methods are realistic and valid for answering the research questions. Progress and outcomes are later judged in terms of how closely work relates to the original proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background and accomplishments of professor and colleagues on project
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants were awarded on the basis of seven criteria: (2) Background and accomplishments of professor and colleagues on project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors consider the principal investigator's and collaborators' academic credentials, prior research record, and demonstrated ability to execute the proposed program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freshness and originality of concept and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants were awarded on the basis of seven criteria: (3) Freshness and originality of concept and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference is given to novel theoretical approaches or methodological innovations; methodological studies that improve measurement sensitivity and validity are explicitly valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential contributions to understanding of advertising, marketing, communication, or consumer behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants were awarded on the basis of seven criteria: (4) Potential contributions to understanding of advertising, marketing, communication, or consumer behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should demonstrate how the research will expand the body of knowledge about advertising and consumers, including theoretical insights and empirical findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Multiplier" capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants were awarded on the basis of seven criteria: (5) "Multiplier" capacity: Will the proposal lead to more doctoral research, published materials, and further study in the field?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funders look for projects that seed additional scholarship (theses, dissertations, publications) and help build ongoing research programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to a total research program vs. special individual project
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants were awarded on the basis of seven criteria: (6) Relation to a total research program vs. special individual project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators consider whether the proposal is part of a coherent, ongoing research program (preferred) rather than an isolated, one-off study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent to which supplementary funds were provided by the school or other sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants were awarded on the basis of seven criteria: (7) Extent to which supplementary funds were provided by the school or other sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals strengthened by institutional commitment or matching/leveraged funds are favored; assess the degree of external or school support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: doctoral students and institutional allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for a grant, a professor had to have one or more doctoral students. The grant was allocated to the school but disbursed at the discretion of the grantee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must demonstrate supervision capacity (doctoral students). Administrative arrangements: awards go to the institution though principal investigator controls disbursement within allowed restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable uses and financial restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants could not cover personal compensation of the grantee or school overhead, and not more than 40% of a grant could be used to compensate faculty members not candidates for degrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget proposals must exclude principal investigator salary and institutional overhead; faculty compensation (outside degree candidates) is capped at 40% of grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant amount limits and renewal policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants were awarded in varying amounts up to $10,000 per year, and a renewal for a second year or beyond could be requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should request realistic budgets ≤ $10,000/year (as historical ceiling) and may request renewals with justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress reporting and evaluation of progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Progress reports were required near the end of the first year, and work accomplished was judged in terms of how closely it related to the original proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim reporting is mandatory; progress is assessed against the original objectives and methods. Continued funding or renewal depends on satisfactory adherence to the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process and advisory oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees were selected by an Academic Advisory Committee, appointed by A.A.A.A. and comprised of five distinguished academicians from the fields of economics, liberal arts, advertising education, and graduate business education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should note the peer-review nature of selection and tailor proposals to the scholarly standards and disciplinary perspectives represented on the committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundation priorities / program goals
rubrics_metrics.description: The Educational Foundation was established to foster six major goals: (1) to create a bridge between advertising and university research, (2) to attract top young people to the study of advertising, (3) to raise the academic stature of advertising, (4) to enlarge the body of knowledge about advertising and the consumer, (5) to document the advertising industry's positions with government, and (6) to work toward establishing chairs of advertising at graduate business schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals aligned with one or more of these goals (especially building academic stature, training graduate students, producing publishable knowledge, and providing impartial research useful to policy) are more likely to be supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of scientific rigor and explicit statement of conditions/generalizability
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic advertising research is expected to produce 'scientific knowledge'—knowledge firmly based on observation, theory, experiments, and yielding predictions; researchers should specify the set of conditions under which their findings hold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals and reports should articulate theoretical grounding, hypotheses, experimental or observational methods, and clearly state the boundary conditions and limits of generalizability so practitioners can judge applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value placed on methodological contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodological studies that investigate new research tools and technology, improve sensitivity and validity of measuring instruments, and develop data analysis procedures are valued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects promising improved measurement techniques, tests, or analytic approaches (e.g., scale development, physiological measures, multivariate methods) are recognized as contributions with wide applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical applicability and caution in transfer to practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: While academic research advances understanding, direct application by practitioners requires caution: findings must be judged for generalizability, and researchers should state explicit conditions; practitioners often need situation-specific investigations to apply results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should consider and articulate how findings could inform practice, including limitations, and, where possible, include plans for applied follow-up or specification of contexts in which results apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for minimal restrictions on funded research
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation's grants were awarded 'with a minimum of restrictions' to encourage broad academic inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should expect autonomy in research conduct, within the administrative and financial constraints (reporting, allowable uses) specified by the Foundation.
